title: Take What You Need
goal: One function is called with an owned String and with a literal. Choose the parameter type that serves both.
hints: String demands every caller manufacture ownership; &String rejects literals outright.
&str accepts &owned by deref coercion AND "ferris" directly - the narrowest type serves the most callers.
explanation: The String parameter taxes both callers: the owned side must clone (or lose `owned` for the final println), the literal side must allocate a String::from. &String fixes one caller and abandons the other - literals aren't &String. &str serves everyone: &owned coerces, "ferris" just works, nothing allocates. Parameter types are pricing policy for your callers - charge the minimum.
